title: Human Oversight in Autonomous DBA Systems

questions.q: In the five-tier oversight spectrum, what distinguishes Tier 3 from Tier 2?
options: Tier 3 executes silently; Tier 2 notifies
Tier 3 is for non-production only
Tier 2 = execute then notify (e.g., index creation on non-production); Tier 3 = proposed, human approval required before execution (e.g., schema migration, major parameter changes)
Tier 3 actions are never allowed in production
questions.explain: Tier 2 is 'automated with real-time notification' (execute, then alert); Tier 3 is 'proposed, human approval required' — queue, wait, execute.

questions.q: The policy engine's resolve_tier escalates the oversight tier when:
options: Confidence is below 0.70, or an incident is active (escalated up to PROPOSE_APPROVE)
The action is in Tier 0
The environment is non-production
The action has 90 days of successful history
questions.explain: resolve_tier raises the tier by one when incident_active (capped at PROPOSE_APPROVE) and when confidence_score < 0.70 (capped at HUMAN_ONLY).

questions.q: Under what conditions may the approval watchdog auto-escalate a pending Tier 3 proposal to Tier 2 (execute-and-notify)?
options: Any proposal older than 1 minute
Pending more than 15 minutes, confidence ≥ 0.85, not yet auto-escalated, and not expired — and only where auto-escalation is explicitly configured per action class
Every proposal, by default, after the SLA deadline passes
Only proposals for DROP TABLE
questions.explain: The watchdog query requires pending > 15 min, confidence ≥ 0.85, tier 3, auto_escalated = 0, expires_at in the future; the chapter stresses auto-escalation is never default-on.

questions.q: Why must approval proposals carry an expiry timestamp?
options: To satisfy a SQL Server data type requirement
Because auditors require timestamps on all rows
To prevent stale approvals from executing actions that are no longer contextually appropriate — e.g., an index build timed for a low-traffic window
To make the proposal table smaller
questions.explain: The chapter states the expiry mechanism is not optional: time-sensitive proposals must expire so a stale approval can't fire when conditions have changed; a fresh proposal is generated for the next window.

questions.q: Which statement about the HUMAN_ONLY tier (Tier 4) is true per the chapter?
options: Its tier is never downgraded by resolve_tier, regardless of context — DROP TABLE, replication topology changes, and cross-region failover stay human-initiated
It can drop to Tier 1 in non-production with 90 days of history
It applies only during business hours
It is the default tier for all new action classes
questions.explain: resolve_tier explicitly forces tier back to HUMAN_ONLY if the base tier is HUMAN_ONLY; it also never automates Tier 4 actions like DROP TABLE regardless of confidence or history.
